tool_args.rationale: All five observations are positive and end at H = 0.48. Over a short window, the slow exponential mostly reveals the ratio of its amplitude to its time constant; different pairs can fit the pilot yet predict different magnitudes or signs at H = 22.8. The probe near H = 20 directly tests that divergence.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled dual-horizon model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The five short-horizon rows cannot reliably separate the slow adaptation amplitude from its time constant, so a good pilot fit would not establish accuracy at H = 22.8.
Finer sampling is less informative about the slow timescale than measurements near the forecast horizon.
It does not constrain the slow adaptation term.
